name: Driftpile Scraplink Utility Belt
description: Heavy-gauge salvaged conveyor webbing, heat-fused at the edges where it frayed, dyed a streaky ochre-brown from industrial runoff exposure. Seven mismatched loops and clips — no two from the same manufacturer — hold everything from wire cutters to ration packs. The buckle is a repurposed mag-lock housing, manually latched. Worn low on the hips, usually over layered shirts. Every mark on it is earned.
functionality: Seven tool loops, two D-ring attachment points, one zippered acid-resistant pouch, and a hidden slit pocket behind the buckle plate. Fits waists 26–48 via field-adjustable lacing at the rear.
what_it_says: This person builds their tools from whatever they can find, and they know exactly where every clip is in the dark.
story_hooks: One of the clips is stamped with a Kelvex MagRail serial number — from a train that derailed four years ago with 200 people aboard.
The hidden slit pocket contains a folded paper note written in a dialect no one in the current district speaks.
A fence offers triple the belt's street value — she wants only the buckle, won't say why.
related_entities: Ringo Heavy Transit MagRail Levitation Transport Network
